title: ReadOutput
description: NDJSON output for read operations with metadata and optional content.

content.description: File content, omitted in stat-only mode or for binary files.

lines.description:
Number of lines in the returned content.

As of v0.1.20 (GAP-2026-008), this is the FILTERED count when a partial
read filter (`--head`, `--tail`, `--line`, `--lines`, `--grep`) is
in effect. The original file total is preserved in `lines_total`.

lines_total.description:
Total lines in the original file before any filter (GAP-2026-008).
Omitted when no filter is applied or the filter did not change the
line count.

truncated.description:
Whether the byte ceiling cut the content (v0.1.39).

Absent when nothing was cut, so a full read keeps its old shape.

next.description: Ready-made command that reads the rest, when the ceiling cut content.

checksum.description: BLAKE3 checksum of the file contents.

binary.description: Whether the file was detected as binary.

range.description: Line range returned when a subset was requested.

verified.description: Checksum verification result, if --verify-checksum was used.

mode.description:
Read mode discriminator (GAP-2026-009): "full" | "head" | "tail" |
"line" | "lines" | "grep" | "stat" | "raw". Allows downstream consumers to
distinguish partial reads from full reads without parsing content.

media.description: What the media channel measured, for a picture or a PDF.

ok.description: Outcome of the run, stamped by the writer

code.description: Machine error code, present when ok is false

exit.description: Process exit status, present when ok is false

target_resolved.description: Absolute targets the run resolved, in invocation order, and never a joined string, so a path holding `,` stays readable; a run with one target publishes a one-item array, so the shape never depends on the count

target_source.description: Where the target came from: named in the invocation line, inherited from the workspace slot, or the standard-input stream

workspace_source.description: Where the workspace root came from: the `--workspace` flag or the process working directory

records_suppressed.description: Records the writer dropped before the terminal event: `--filter` rejections, `--select` projections that emptied the record, dedupe duplicates and `--limit` cuts. It counts records, never files, so it does not compare with `files_matched`: one file can contribute several records

files_budget_dropped.description: Entries the `--limit` budget dropped, in the unit the verb produces: files for walking verbs, records for streaming ones; a floor, because workers may stop before producing the rest

files_planned.description: Files the run would have modified in `--dry-run` or `--preview`; absent from a run that really wrote

truncated_records.description: Records the writer cut this run, counted once per record

LineRange.description: Inclusive 1-based line range for partial file reads.

MediaInfo.description: Facts about a picture or a PDF page set, measured before delivery.

width.description: Picture width after orientation, absent for a PDF.

height.description: Picture height after orientation, absent for a PDF.

format.description: Format named by the magic bytes, or `pdf`.

visual_tokens.description: Visual tokens the delivered picture costs.

needs_vision.description: Pages that carry no text and therefore need the drawn page.
